name: Obal
overview: Obal is a male figure in Scripture identified primarily as the son of Joktan, as recorded in Genesis 10:28. Beyond this direct lineage, there is no further tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about his life or role. His mention situates him within the genealogical records of the descendants of Noah, emphasizing his place in biblical history.
namesAndTitles: The name Obal appears as a proper name in Genesis 10:28 without a given meaning or divine origin. Additionally, the name Ebal is listed as an alternative form in 1 Chronicles 1:22, also without a specified meaning. Both names are simple proper names used in genealogical contexts.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Obal as a son of Joktan, establishing a direct father-son relationship. No other family relationships are recorded in the biblical text beyond this connection, limiting our understanding of his broader familial context.
scriptureSignificance: Obal's significance lies in his inclusion in the genealogical account of Joktan's descendants, which traces the post-Flood repopulation of the earth. Though not elaborated upon, his mention contributes to the biblical record of nations and peoples originating from Noah's lineage. This genealogical listing underscores God's providential preservation and multiplication of humanity through chosen family lines.
